importance_ranking.reason: Location (city/micromarket), property type, and capacity are the primary shortlisting gates — a buyer cannot evaluate any listing without confirming these three dimensions match their requirement. Wrong city or wrong workspace format = immediate skip regardless of all other signals.

Workspace ambience, fit-out quality, and modernity are significant purchase signals — buyers shortlist based on visual appeal of the space, and a listing with no image or a poor-quality image loses credibility immediately in a category where the physical environment is the product.

price_display_type.determination_note: Office space price varies substantially by property type (coworking hot desk vs private managed office), capacity tier, furnishing status, and city/micromarket — buyers cannot meaningfully compare prices without knowing the spec configuration, making spec the primary price driver, with regional variance (city and micromarket) as a strong secondary modifier.

importance_ranking.reason: Indian B2B buyers are price-aggressive and compare per-seat or per-sq-ft rates across operators; price is a hard shortlisting gate after location, type, and capacity confirm fit, and the listed rate is the primary basis for initial engagement.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Two coexisting units in this MCAT: per seat/month (coworking/flex) and per sq ft/month (traditional lease/sale). Mixing these without labelling creates direct price comparison errors — a buyer comparing a per-seat quote with a per-sq-ft quote cannot assess value without the unit. Per seat/month is dominant for the primary segment (flex/coworking); per sq ft/month applies to traditional lease and sale transactions.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listing types without knowing the unit — per seat/month vs per sq ft/month is a real market ambiguity that causes buyers to misread value; unit must always be shown alongside price in this category.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Recognised flex operators (WeWork India, Awfis, Regus, Smartworks, IndiQube, 91 Springboard) carry brand weight as quality and reliability signals; enterprise buyers actively specify or prefer named operators, and ownership type (direct owner vs broker) is a trust signal for traditional lease listings.
importance_ranking.reason: Operator brand is a meaningful trust and quality signal in the premium flex segment, and direct-owner vs broker distinction affects negotiation and reliability confidence for traditional lease buyers — company ranks last but is not irrelevant.
